assessments.closureRisk: Low-to-moderate; internally closable, but risk that variants are not materially different enough to discriminate.
assessments.dominantCost: Experiment design and re-running causal-episode probes across multiple variants.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Create 2-3 materially different Scenario/Genesis encounter variants and re-run causal-episode probes across them; classify each prior as surviving or overfit.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: AF002's surviving priors are partly overfit to the single fixed Genesis; variant perturbations will separate robust causal priors from fixed-encounter artifacts.

assessments.closureRisk: Low; highly closable but low marginal research value.
assessments.dominantCost: Mechanical gate execution and release ceremony.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Run final portable and physical gates, commit exact P5 source, graduate through structured self-release.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Mechanism selection is complete; remaining work is exact final acceptance and release, low research novelty.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Near-closeout mechanical work with minimal frontier delta; budget better spent on open research question in G-AF3.

assessments.closureRisk: Moderate; value contingent on finding a measurable packaging win.
assessments.dominantCost: Import-graph audit and packaging candidate construction; uncertain payoff.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Audit Host import/dependency graph; build smallest packaging candidate only if measurable; dogfood against World and another non-MCP consumer.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: A narrower core/domain/extension install surface may be justifiable, but semantic compatibility already passed; value depends on whether packaging cost is measurable.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Uncertain payoff — only justified if a measurable narrower surface exists; lower expected value than G-AF3's direct generalization experiment.

assessments.closureRisk: High; externally blocked despite admitted repair.
assessments.dominantCost: External DNS dependency; cannot proceed until recovery.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Retry no-tool incremental after DNS recovery; run replay/batch and resolved-provider controls; compare utilization and decision quality.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Control-path repair is causally admitted but live experiments remain externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery; not closable now regardless of admitted repair.

assessments.closureRisk: Very high; entirely externally blocked, cannot close now.
assessments.operatorPolicy: Obtain independent Linux/systemd host; verify immutable deployment kit; provision purpose-separated signers and executor-only Trade credential.
assessments.topologyHypothesis: Negative control; dominant blocker is absence of an independently administered Linux/systemd host, which the current WSL/Windows workstation cannot satisfy.
assessments.whyNotFirst: Deferred — dominant blocker is external infrastructure acquisition with no in-reach path to closure this cycle.

result.choiceRationale: G-AF3 is the strongest candidate: AF002 is complete, the current fixed Genesis has almost no environment variation, and the next step (materially different encounter variants) is a well-defined, internally-closable experiment that directly earns robustness/generalization claims — a frontier delta of prior-generalization or defect-discovery. It is not externally blocked. R-P5 is near-closeout but its remaining work is mostly mechanical (final gates, commit, release) with low marginal research value; HOST-PKG is a packaging/import-graph audit whose value is uncertain and only justified if a measurable candidate emerges; H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery despite an admitted control-path repair; F-C2-BLOCKED is a negative control whose dominant blocker (no independent Linux/systemd host) is entirely external and non-closable now — deferred.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether G-AF3's variant-perturbation experiments separate surviving causal priors from fixed-encounter overfit, i.e., whether the frontier delta lands as prior-generalization (surviving priors) vs defect-discovery (overfit exposed).
result.selectionFalsifier: If G-AF3's variant construction turns out to be blocked by an unadmitted external dependency (e.g., engine/scenario tooling unavailable), or if the perturbations are not "materially different" enough to discriminate overfit from generalization, then the choice would be falsified and R-P5 (closable, low-risk) would have been the safer allocation.
